states.changed: A visitor meets the world's counted AI chips as 2,092 squares and reads them four ways: who holds them, who votes over the holders, who uses them, and where a public stands.

Reading 3 now draws the Field's record of use: each holder carries the developers that name it as provider, OpenAI and Anthropic stand with no square; reading 4 no longer reads a missing public row as zero; a fifth reading lets the visitor choose whom they would hold answerable and lights how much of the stock the record lets that answer name.

The five firms' rise from 56.6 % to 68.6 % of the counted chips now stands above the squares in fixed text and bars; 'who uses' marks holders that build on their own chips (Google, Meta, xAI) beside those that rent; reading 4 became 'where law appears' (the smuggled category and the suspension orders in CoreWeave's filed contracts) instead of a missing public owner, and the visitor can now choose 'a court or regulator'.

Reading 4 now marks the chips that Google, Meta and xAI keep for their own models (37.8 % of the counted stock) as held inside the firm, where nothing changes hands and no contract could carry a law, with xAI's filed right to take rented capacity back; a reach-outside reading of Coase's Nobel lecture divides 'control' into what is traded and what is planned, and the work is presented.
